title: Square gauges: First qualifying slip
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: For each nonnegative reading x, produce the greatest integer r with r*r <= x. Use integer comparisons rather than floating-point rounding. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
A square inspection plate must fit inside each numbered sheet allowance using whole-unit edges. Luz needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

For each nonnegative reading x, produce the greatest integer r with r*r <= x. Use integer comparisons rather than floating-point rounding.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement squareGaugesFirstQualifyingSlip(readings, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Binary search on answers. For each nonnegative reading x, produce the greatest integer r with r*r <= x. Use integer comparisons rather than floating-point rounding. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.

Target time O(n log M); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with binary search on answers. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each nonnegative reading x, produce the greatest integer r with r*r <= x. Use integer comparisons rather than floating-point rounding. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
